Record letters in the order spoken.

blocks.title: D03-OPEN: Who followed the word limit?
blocks.mode: Written compliance check; individual commitment, then explanation. This checks instruction knowledge, not listening performance.
blocks.instructions: Instruction: Write ONE WORD ONLY from "walking boots". Who has followed the word limit?

blocks.title: D03-MODEL: Final detail and spelling
blocks.mode: Teacher read, guided; teacher reads the two model lines once; learners answer before the reveal
blocks.instructions: Listen to your teacher. Answer each question before the reveal.

stimulus.title: Model lines (teacher reads once)
paragraphs: We planned to meet at 8.20, but the building opens later. Please meet at 8.50 instead.
The tutor is Ms Benton. That's B-E-N-T-O-N.

items.prompt: Tutor's surname? Write ONE WORD ONLY.
items.reason: Ignore capitalization; preserve the exact spelling.

blocks.title: D03-A: School science display
blocks.mode: Round A: play once, answers committed, then one optional full replay. Record actual replays; do not count the replay as fresh evidence.
blocks.instructions: Questions A1–A5: Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer. Question A6: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS. Complete the notes.

stimulus.title: Private script A — all dialogue is fictional
paragraphs: Student: I'd like to help with the school science display. When is it?
Coordinator: The display is in November. We are collecting project ideas during October, but the display itself is the following month.
Student: Who is leading the project?
Coordinator: Ms Bramwell. That's B-R-A-M-W-E-L-L, with two Ls at the end.
Student: What time should our team meet?
Coordinator: Meet at nine forty in the morning to arrange your display. Visitors can enter from ten fifteen, so you'll have time to prepare.
Student: How many teams are taking part?
Coordinator: Twelve teams, with two students in each. That makes twenty-four students altogether, but just twelve separate displays.
Student: Do we need to buy paper and glue?
Coordinator: The school will provide paper. Please bring glue; we do not have enough for every team. You won't need any other materials.
Student: Where will we prepare everything? In the gym?
Coordinator: We had planned to use the gym, but a class needs it. Go to the art room for preparation. The display will be in the hall.

items.reason: October is for collecting ideas, not the display.

items.evidence: That's B-R-A-M-W-E-L-L, with two Ls at the end.
Meet at nine forty in the morning to arrange your display.
items.reason: Nine forty is preparation; ten fifteen is visitor entry.

items.evidence: Twelve teams, with two students in each.
items.reason: Twelve teams, not twenty-four individual students.

items.evidence: Please bring glue; we do not have enough for every team.
items.reason: Paper is provided; students must bring glue.
items.focus: explicit detail; supplied versus required material

items.evidence: Go to the art room for preparation.
items.reason: Replaces the gym for preparation; the hall is for the display.

blocks.marking: One point per item for classroom feedback only. Do not penalize punctuation in numeric times. Read the preprinted units; do not require "a.m." again. Other forms require teacher review rather than a newly invented automatic spelling/number normalization.

blocks.title: D03-B: Media room booking
blocks.mode: Round B: play once; commit, then optional full replay. Record help.
blocks.instructions: Questions B1–B3: Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER. Question B4: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.

stimulus.title: Private script B
paragraphs: Student: I'm calling about our media room booking.
Assistant: Yes. You'll use room three eighteen. Room three thirteen is being used for a staff meeting.
Student: Will Mr Palmer supervise us?
Assistant: He cannot come that day. Ms Vale will supervise. Her surname is V-A-L-E.
Student: I requested fifty minutes. Has that been confirmed?
Assistant: We've only been able to reserve thirty-five minutes. Another group needs the room after that.
Student: Do we need our headphones?
Assistant: No, the room has headphones you can borrow. Each student must bring a memory card to save the recording.

items.reason: Room 313 is for staff. "Three eighteen" exceeds the one-word limit.
Final confirmed detail: Mr Palmer cannot come that day.

items.evidence: We've only been able to reserve thirty-five minutes.
Each student must bring a memory card to save the recording.

blocks.marking: Numeric forms are preferred. Written number forms above are accepted for this classroom draft; register exact normalization before any server marking. Do not merge Round A, Round B, replays and corrections into independent checks.

stages.title: Opening challenge: the word limit
stages.student: Decide which learner followed the word limit. Commit before the explanation.
stages.teacher: Opening challenge. Individual commitment, then explanation.
stages.say: Write ONE WORD ONLY from "walking boots". Who has followed the word limit?
stages.check: Every learner has chosen Learner A or Learner B before the explanation.

stages.title: Model: the final detail and the spelling
stages.student: Listen to the two model lines and answer before the reveal.
stages.teacher: Model. Teacher reads the two model lines once; pupils answer before reveal.
stages.say: Listen once. Write the meeting time and the tutor's surname.
stages.check: Learners have written both answers before the reveal.

stages.title: Round A: read the questions
stages.student: Read questions A1 to A6 and the two word limits. Predict the answer type, not the answer.
stages.teacher: Read Round A questions; predict answer type, not the answer.
stages.say: What kind of answer does each gap need: a month, a name, a time, a number or a thing?
stages.check: Learners can say which questions allow two words.

stages.title: Round A: listen and commit
stages.student: Listen once and write your answers. Commit them before any replay.
stages.teacher: Round A once, answers committed, then one optional full replay. Record actual replays; do not count the replay as fresh evidence.
stages.say: Write your answers while you listen. Keep your first answers.
stages.check: Answers are committed; any replay is recorded.

stages.title: Round A: answers and evidence
stages.student: Check each answer against the evidence. Preserve your first answers and correct beside them.
stages.teacher: Reveal A1–A6; students check the precise support (quoted on the reveal slides) only after listening is complete. Preserve first answers.
stages.say: Which detail was the final one? Which detail did you reject?
stages.check: Learners can explain one rejected detail.

stages.title: Round B: read the questions
stages.student: Read questions B1 to B4. Compare the two instruction lines.
stages.teacher: Read Round B questions and compare the two instruction lines.
stages.say: Which question allows two words? Which questions allow a number?
stages.check: Learners can name the question that allows two words.

stages.title: Round B: listen and commit
stages.student: Listen once and write your answers. Commit them before any replay.
stages.teacher: Round B once; commit, then optional full replay. Record help.
stages.say: Write your answers while you listen. Keep your first answers.
stages.check: Answers are committed; any help or replay is recorded.

stages.title: Round B: answers and evidence
stages.student: Check each answer: final detail, spelling and answer length.
stages.teacher: Reveal B1–B4. Discuss final detail, spelling and answer length.
stages.say: Does your answer keep to the word limit? Is it the final confirmed detail?
stages.check: Learners can explain why "three eighteen" does not fit the limit.

stages.title: Targeted support
stages.student: Work on the support activity your teacher gives you, or explain one error in writing.
stages.teacher: Teacher selects one support activity (D03-S1, D03-S2 or D03-S3, printed from Support_Activities.pdf); others explain one error or write a concise note about a misleading detail.
stages.say: Choose one answer you changed. Explain the error using the recording evidence.
stages.check: Each learner has either a support sheet or a written explanation of one error.

stages.title: Exit reflection
stages.student: Identify one corrected response and explain why.
stages.teacher: Exit reflection: identify one corrected response and explain why. This is a reflection, not another listening assessment.
stages.say: Which answer did you correct today, and why?

stages.title: Homework and next step
stages.student: Copy down the homework. Agree one next step with your teacher.
stages.teacher: Assign written homework and agree one next step.
stages.say: At home, check every answer against its word limit before you finish.
stages.check: Everyone has the homework sheet and one next step.
